evidence: Byte-level blob comparison shows every staged picap, a11y, whatsapp, parser, model and eval file identical to the refactor parent, and MainActivity.kt, SavedLocationsScreen.kt, SavedLocationManager.kt, AndroidManifest.xml and build.gradle.kts identical to HEAD, with no unmerged paths and no conflict markers in any staged blob; the four result files and build evidence were rewritten as one set describing this merge, resolving the mixed-lineage artifact set.

The merged shell keeps both routes: Picap events go to offerProcessor.handlePicapEvent and WhatsApp or WhatsApp Biz events go to whatsappResponder.handleWhatsAppEvent, the instance, pasteAndSend, pasteOnly and hasTextInput facade members used by WhatsAppForwardActivity are all still defined, and a cross-file scan found no call to any function removed when MyAccessibilityService was slimmed.

NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS is declared exactly once as 200L in PicapOfferCloser.kt and read from PicapOfferCloser and PicapOfferProcessor, evaluateAutoAccept is imported and invoked from PicapAutoAcceptPolicy, WhatsAppResponder and NotificationInterceptorService, a declaration scan of all 35 Kotlin files found no duplicate top-level type, val or fun name inside the same package, and the build evidence records a full rerun with all 35 tasks executed ending BUILD SUCCESSFUL on versionCode 64 versionName 0.3.49.

findings.claim: The merge activates a WhatsApp auto-accept widening relative to HEAD. Both call sites now pass 999.0 when the pickup km cannot be parsed, and evaluator condition 3 accepts whenever the km switch is on and the threshold is 5.0 or greater, so a km-less or malformed message is auto-accepted where HEAD required a non-null km. This is the user-approved Picap-parity behavior documented on the refactor lineage.
proof_refs: HEAD MyAccessibilityService.kt line 591 guarded condition 3 with kmRecogida not null, while staged WhatsAppResponder.kt line 136 and NotificationInterceptorService.kt line 162 substitute 999.0 before calling evaluateAutoAccept.

AutoAcceptEvaluator.kt line 66 returns accepted for condition 3 when the km switch is enabled and maxKm is at least 5.0 without reading the km argument, so the 999.0 sentinel always satisfies that branch.
The change carries an explanatory comment in the refactor parent, but it is behavior-activated by this merge against HEAD and enlarges the set of messages that trigger auto-respond.
